summary: 64-byte UI command stack: a three-word header (target, flags, object) followed by four 12-byte command entries and a depth counter at +0x3C, popped one command per frame by Ui_CommandQueue_Advance.
evidence: Ui_CommandQueue_Advance (0x006D7200) reads queue[0xF] as the depth, indexes entries as `queue + depth*3` words (Ui_CommandQueue_FindEntry uses `queue + f_3c*0xC` bytes), releases `*queue` through func_0010EBD8 and broadcasts the next entry. The 4 entry blocks of 3 words occupy +0xC..+0x3B and the depth sits at +0x3C, so the 64-byte size is exact. AdvanceAlt (0x006D7F34) is instruction-identical and all its callers are Ui_SakusenWindow_* helpers.

fields.name: commandTarget
fields.evidence: queue[1] is called directly (`(*pcVar2)()`); when bit 0 of queue[2] is set it is instead treated as an object and a code pointer is read as `*(code**)(pcVar2 + *(int*)(*queue + (queue[2]>>1)))`, so it is either a plain callback or an object/table base - the dual use blocks a more specific name

fields.name: commandFlags
fields.evidence: bit 0 (=1) selects the indirect dispatch branch and queue[2] is compared with the requested flags in Ui_CommandQueue_FindEntry, with a special case for command id 0 + bit 0

fields.name: depth
fields.evidence: queue[0xF] is decremented after each pop, 0 means empty, and it multiplies the entry stride (`queue[queue[0xf]*3]`, and `queue + queue->f_3c*0xC` bytes in FindEntry)
